quote: The amended § 11.2 (effective for claims arising on or after September 21, 2026) excludes only: (a) Supplier's indemnity for **third-party IP claims** (§ 9.1(c)) ... **Recall costs are no longer excluded from the cap.** The cap is "fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose" (§ 11.1). ... This means the following indemnity claims are now **subject to the six-month fee cap**: § 9.1(a): Product defects or nonconformity; § 9.1(b): Personal injury, death, or property damage caused by the Products
reason: Issues 3 and 4 together cover the criterion. The memo identifies that Amendment No. 1 § 2 (cited as § 2.1) replaces Supply Agreement § 11.2. It shows that recall costs are dropped from the carve-outs and that the indemnity carve-out is narrowed to third-party IP claims under § 9.1(c). It explains that recall and product-liability/personal-injury exposure is now capped at six months of fees, and says why this matters to Harrowgate. The memo also recommends restoring the original § 11.2.
